newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity moves two fund groups to N.H. from Dallas.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity moves two fund groups to N.H. from Dallas.

text.p: Fidelity Investments said it will move its fixed-income mutual fund group from Boston and its money market fund group from Dallas to Merrimack, N.H. next year, impacting 320 jobs.
Fidelity spokesman Andy Trincia said the Boston-based company is still evaluating how many employees will make the move.
"These are growing units; they need space and room to grow. One of the reasons we went to New Hampshire in the first place is the pro-business atmosphere there," Trincia said.

Fidelity originally planned to move the fixed-income group to Smithfield, Rhode Island. Fidelity is still committed to moving jobs down the Smithfield by 1998 and eventually employing 2,500 people there, he said.
After the move, Fidelity will still employ more than 2,600 people in Dallas in phone services, retirement services, technical support and a number of other units, Trincia said.
